title: Getting Started with ccreds
text: generate data censored-covariate regression model \(n = 200\) observations \(p = 10\) features. Response-variable model: \[y_i = \beta_0 + \alpha x_i + \boldsymbol{\beta}^\top \mathbf{z}_i + \varepsilon_i, \quad \varepsilon_i \sim N(0, \sigma^2)\] Censored-covariate model: \[X_i \mid \mathbf{z}_i \sim \chi^2(\mu_i), \quad \mu_i = \exp(\gamma_0 + \boldsymbol{\gamma}^\top \mathbf{z}_i)\] set \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\) \(\boldsymbol{\gamma}\) sparse partially overlapping support, features affect response, affect censored covariate, affect .
code: set.seed(8371)  n <- 200 p <- 10  # Correlated features (AR(0.5) structure) rho <- 0.5 Sigma <- 9 * toeplitz(rho^(0:(p - 1))) z <- mvrnorm(n = n, mu = rep(0, p), Sigma = Sigma)  # True parameters beta_0 <- 5 alpha <- 10 beta <- c(4, 4, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, -2, -4) sigma_sq <- 100  gamma_0 <- 2 gamma <- c(0, 0.04, 0.04, 0.02, 0.02, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)  # Generate the censored covariate x x_mean <- exp(cbind(1, z) %*% c(gamma_0, gamma)) |> drop() x <- rchisq(n, df = x_mean)  # Generate censoring times to achieve ~50% censoring compute_c_mean <- function(censoring_rate, x_mean) {   f <- function(c_mean) {     1 - pbeta(0.5, x_mean / 2, c_mean / 2) - censoring_rate   }   uniroot(f, lower = 1e-12, upper = 1000)$root } c_mean <- vapply(x_mean, \(m) compute_c_mean(0.5, m), numeric(1)) cens <- rchisq(n, df = c_mean)  # Generate response e <- rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(sigma_sq)) y <- cbind(1, x, z) %*% c(beta_0, alpha, beta) + e  # Observed covariate and censoring indicator w <- pmin(x, cens) d <- as.numeric(x <= cens)  # Assemble the data frame in the format ccreds() expects z_df <- as.data.frame(z) colnames(z_df) <- paste0("z", 1:p) dat <- tibble(   case = 1:n,   y = drop(y),   w = w,   d = d ) |>   bind_cols(z_df)  dat #> # A tibble: 200 × 14 #>     case      y     w     d     z1     z2     z3     z4     z5      z6     z7 #>    <int>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl> #>  1     1 175.    9.22     0  0.864  5.58  -2.49  -4.58  -2.22  -5.77   -7.38  #>  2     2  51.4   4.07     1  3.97   0.563 -1.88  -5.91  -4.88  -3.98   -1.80  #>  3     3  57.4   3.67     1 -3.31  -0.249 -1.47  -0.337  2.50  -4.96   -0.888 #>  4     4   4.85  3.27     0 -5.07  -3.71  -0.419 -1.84  -3.11  -0.662   0.492 #>  5     5  98.2   7.09     1 -1.24   3.01  -1.35  -5.48  -1.32   0.410  -1.66  #>  6     6 171.   12.4      1  2.81   3.71   3.79  -1.13   0.975  4.29    4.29  #>  7     7 187.   15.5      1 -1.43   6.47   5.36   1.81   2.97  -0.472   0.580 #>  8     8 131.    3.71     0  1.07  -0.824 -1.11  -2.99  -1.73  -8.31   -3.22  #>  9     9  85.1   2.64     0  1.61  -1.60   0.470  0.377  1.03  -0.0646 -3.84  #> 10    10 256.    9.71     0 -1.53  -0.207  3.47   3.52   2.03   0.945   1.39  #> # ℹ 190 more rows #> # ℹ 3 more variables: z8 <dbl>, z9 <dbl>, z10 <dbl> mean(dat$d == 0) #> [1] 0.445

text: best \((\lambda_1, \lambda_2)\) pair chosen minimising cross-validated mean absolute error response, CV_MAE_y. can inspect estimated coefficients compare truth:
code: best <- results |> slice_min(CV_MAE_y, n = 1) best |> select(lambda_1, lambda_2, CV_MAE_y) #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   lambda_1 lambda_2 CV_MAE_y #>      <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1     0.01     0.01     35.0  fit <- best$full_fit[[1]] # Response-model coefficients tibble(   feature = paste0("z", 1:p),   true_beta = beta,   estimated_beta = round(fit$beta, 3) ) #> # A tibble: 10 × 3 #>    feature true_beta estimated_beta #>    <chr>       <dbl>          <dbl> #>  1 z1              4           3.53 #>  2 z2              4           3.77 #>  3 z3              2           1.89 #>  4 z4              0           0    #>  5 z5              0           0    #>  6 z6              0           0    #>  7 z7              0           0    #>  8 z8              0           0    #>  9 z9             -2          -2.42 #> 10 z10            -4          -3.27  # Censored-covariate coefficients tibble(   feature = paste0("z", 1:p),   true_gamma = gamma,   estimated_gamma = round(fit$gamma, 5) ) #> # A tibble: 10 × 3 #>    feature true_gamma estimated_gamma #>    <chr>        <dbl>           <dbl> #>  1 z1            0           -0.00367 #>  2 z2            0.04         0.0541  #>  3 z3            0.04         0.0398  #>  4 z4            0.02         0.0441  #>  5 z5            0.02        -0.0083  #>  6 z6            0            0.0180  #>  7 z7            0           -0.0195  #>  8 z8            0            0.00905 #>  9 z9            0           -0.0135  #> 10 z10           0            0.00144

title: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection
text: ccreds R package performing Censored-Covariate Regression Dual Selection. ccreds allows users fit penalised censored-covariate regression models two separate L1 penalties — one selecting features associated response variable one selecting features associated censored covariate. Tuning parameters selected via cross-validation. Functions producing visual diagnostics cross-validation heat maps, coefficient paths, plotting estimated densities, provided.

title: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection
text: main function ccreds(). Input data must data frame columns order: output tibble one row per (lambda_1, lambda_2) pair, containing cross-validation metrics full model fit. extract best model: parallel computation lambda grid: requires future furrr packages.
code: library(ccreds)  results <- ccreds(   data = my_data,   lambda_1s = c(0.01, 0.1, 1),   lambda_2s = c(0.01, 0.1, 1),   k = 5 ) best <- results |> dplyr::slice_min(CV_MAE_y) fit <- best$full_fit[[1]]  fit$beta_0    # Intercept (beta_0) fit$alpha     # Coefficient of censored covariate x (alpha) fit$beta      # Feature coefficients for y (beta vector) fit$sigma_sq  # Error variance (sigma^2) fit$gamma_0   # Intercept for x model (gamma_0) fit$gamma     # Feature coefficients for x (gamma vector) results <- ccreds(   data = my_data,   lambda_1s = c(0.01, 0.1, 1),   lambda_2s = c(0.01, 0.1, 1),   cores = 4 )

title: ccreds: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection — ccreds-package
text: Implements penalised observed-data log-likelihood method feature selection censored-covariate regression models. Uses two separate L1 penalties select features associated response variable features associated censored covariate, via Expectation-Minimisation (EM) algorithm. Tuning parameters chosen cross-validation.

text: Fits penalised censored-covariate regression models grid tuning parameters \((\lambda_1, \lambda_2)\) using cross-validation evaluate prediction performance. pair, EM algorithm estimates model parameters applying \(L_1\) penalties perform feature selection response-variable model component censored-covariate model component.

title: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection — ccreds
code: ccreds(   data,   lambda_1s,   lambda_2s,   force_active_beta = integer(0),   force_active_gamma = integer(0),   k = 5,   cores = 1 )

title: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection — ccreds
text: data data frame columns order: case (integer ID), y (response), w (observed value x censoring time), d (censoring indicator: 1 = observed, 0 = censored), z1, z2, ..., zp (features). lambda_1s Numeric vector candidate values \(\lambda_1\), penalty \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\). lambda_2s Numeric vector candidate values \(\lambda_2\), penalty \(\boldsymbol{\gamma}\). force_active_beta Integer vector feature indices (referring z column numbers) penalised \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\). Default integer(0). force_active_gamma Integer vector feature indices penalised \(\boldsymbol{\gamma}\). Default integer(0). k Number cross-validation folds. Default 5. cores Number parallel workers. greater 1, uses future furrr parallel computation. Default 1.

title: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection — ccreds
text: tibble one row per \((\lambda_1, \lambda_2)\) pair columns: lambda_1, lambda_2 tuning parameter values. full_fit list containing fitted model full data, elements: beta_0 Intercept \(\beta_0\). alpha Coefficient \(\alpha\) censored covariate \(x\). beta Feature coefficient vector \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\) length \(p\). sigma_sq Error variance \(\sigma^2\). gamma_0 Intercept \(\gamma_0\). gamma Feature coefficient vector \(\boldsymbol{\gamma}\) length \(p\). beta_selected Number non-zero entries \(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}\) (excluding forced-active features). gamma_selected Number non-zero entries \(\hat{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\) (excluding forced-active features). iterations Number EM iterations convergence. CV_MAE_y Cross-validated mean absolute error \(y\). CV_MAE_y_SE Standard error CV_MAE_y across folds. CV_MAE_x Cross-validated mean absolute error \(x\) (computed complete observations ). CV_MAE_x_SE Standard error CV_MAE_x across folds. time Elapsed time fitting lambda pair.

title: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection — ccreds
text: censored-covariate regression model consists two components: Response-variable model: $$y_i = \beta_0 + \alpha x_i + \boldsymbol{\beta}^\top   \mathbf{z}_i + \varepsilon_i, \quad \varepsilon_i \sim N(0,   \sigma^2)$$ Censored-covariate model: $$X_i \mid \mathbf{z}_i \sim \chi^2(\mu_i), \quad \mu_i =   \exp(\gamma_0 + \boldsymbol{\gamma}^\top \mathbf{z}_i)$$ \(\beta_0\) \(\gamma_0\) intercepts, \(\alpha\) coefficient censored covariate \(x\), \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\) \(\boldsymbol{\gamma}\) feature coefficient vectors subject \(L_1\) penalisation.

title: Plot coefficient paths — plot_coefficient_paths
text: Shows estimated feature coefficients \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\) \(\boldsymbol{\gamma}\) change corresponding penalty parameter varies. component = "beta", plot varies \(\lambda_1\) holding \(\lambda_2\) fixed, vice versa component = "gamma".

title: Plot coefficient paths — plot_coefficient_paths
code: plot_coefficient_paths(   results,   component = c("beta", "gamma"),   lambda_fixed = NULL,   feature_names = NULL,   highlight = TRUE )

title: Plot coefficient paths — plot_coefficient_paths
text: results tibble returned ccreds(). component Either "beta" "gamma". lambda_fixed value held-fixed penalty. NULL (default), uses value minimum CV_MAE_y row. feature_names Optional character vector length \(p\) giving display names features. NULL, uses z1, z2, etc. highlight Logical; TRUE (default), highlights features non-zero minimum-CV model adds dashed vertical line chosen penalty value.

title: Plot predictive densities — plot_density
text: Plots joint density \(f(y, x \mid \mathbf{z})\) filled contour, , y_given supplied, overlays marginal density \(f(x \mid \mathbf{z})\) conditional density \(f(x \mid \mathbf{z}, y)\) specific value \(y\).

title: Plot predictive densities — plot_density
code: plot_density(   fit,   z,   x_range = NULL,   y_range = NULL,   y_given = NULL,   n_grid = 200 )

title: Plot predictive densities — plot_density
text: fit single fitted model list (e.g. one element full_fit column ccreds() output), containing beta_0, alpha, beta, sigma_sq, gamma_0, gamma. z Numeric vector feature values (length \(p\)). x_range Numeric vector length 2 giving range \(x\) values plot. Default computed chi-squared distribution implied model. y_range Numeric vector length 2 giving range \(y\) values (used joint contour plot). Default computed model. y_given Optional scalar. supplied, produces density overlay \(f(x \mid \mathbf{z})\) \(f(x \mid \mathbf{z}, y = y_{given})\) instead joint contour. n_grid Number grid points per axis. Default 200.

title: Plot predictive densities — plot_density
text: ggplot object.
